clue.text: Part of the artichoke

indicators.note: only a part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters lying inside them

parts.note: the run of letters starting at the second letter of the first word

explanation.surface: A simple description of one piece of a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the answer is sitting inside 'the artichoke', and is also the tender centre of that vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleshy edible centre of a globe artichoke is called its heart, and it is sold under that name.

clue.text: Screen the first two-thirds of 80s sit-com

indicators.note: keeping only the first two-thirds means the final third is cut off

parts.note: Hi-de-Hi! was a BBC sitcom of the 1980s set in a holiday camp

explanation.surface: Show part of an old 1980s television comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Screen looks like showing a programme; it is a verb meaning to conceal. Hi-de-Hi! is a British holiday-camp sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to shield it from view, which is to hide it.

clue.text: Blast to Saturn with a spaceman

indicators.note: a blast blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the second a in the clue

explanation.surface: A rocket launch sends a crew member off to Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like a rocket blast-off; it is the signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a person trained to travel in space.

clue.text: A crowd on the decking

indicators.note: decking something means covering or adorning it, so the article wraps around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
re means on the subject of

explanation.surface: Too many people are standing on the wooden deck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'. Decking looks like a timber floor; here it means adorning.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes the number a crowd in crossword terms.

clue.text: Pleased with Sierra and Fiesta I'd fixed

parts.note: Sierra is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for S

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rigged, so these letters are put back together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is happy with their two Ford cars, a Sierra and a Fiesta, now that the Fiesta has been repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra and Fiesta are both Ford models, which makes the car scene convincing; Sierra is really just the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: To be satisfied is to be content or gratified, the same state as being pleased.

clue.text: Suspect a cleptomaniac's smuggling picture

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something concealed, so the answer is tucked away inside these words

parts.note: the letters run from the third letter of the first word into the third word

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a thief with a stealing compulsion of sneaking out a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' looks like a stolen artwork; it is the definition, as in 'what a picture she made'. The setter uses the variant spelling cleptomaniac to make the letters fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking sight or display, as a picture can be in the sense of a vivid scene.

clue.text: At both sides of Toyota — left and right

indicators.note: only both sides, the two ends, are wanted, so the middle of the car maker's name is dropped

parts.note: the Japanese car maker, whose two middle letters go
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A Toyota car has been damaged on both sides, left and right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left and right' sounds like the two sides of the car; 'right' is the British intensifier, as in 'a right mess'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a right idiot is a complete or utter idiot, so right can mean absolute.

clue.text: Underwater mobile article put in the sea with American backing

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the abbreviation is read from the end

parts.note: US stands for the United States, so American

indicators.note: putting something in a place means placing it inside, so these letters go into the next word

parts.note: the briny is the sea, from its salt water
Chambers gives M for mobile, as in mobile phone services
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A mobile phone item is thrown into the sea, backed by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: The M for mobile is unusual but is in the Chambers dictionary. The wordplay order is reversed: SU comes first though 'American backing' ends the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine is also an adjective meaning existing or operating beneath the sea's surface.

clue.text: Movie stars I see on the front of Sight and Sound

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the verb is used only for its sound, which matches the name of a letter

parts.note: the word is said like the letter's name
taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, and both of these words share the same opening

parts.note: both words begin with the same letter

explanation.surface: Someone spots film stars on the cover of Sight and Sound, the British film magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sight and Sound is a long-running British film magazine, which makes the movie scene convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are celebrated figures who are widely admired, as big film stars are.

clue.text: Power-dressed woman spilled martini after party, getting cross

indicators.note: after places the cocktail's letters second, behind the word for a party that ends the clue phrase

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: a spilled drink splashes out of shape, so these letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: A woman in a power suit spills her martini after a party and gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: Power-dressing usually means business suits; here it is a woman dressed to wield power in a sexual role. Cross looks like angry but is X.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominatrix is a woman who takes the dominant role in sadomasochistic sex, typically dressed in leather.

clue.text: Cleaner and I abandoning German beside public toilet scratching backside

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is taken out of the name that follows
scratching out the backside means rubbing off the rear end, the final letter

parts.note: Dieter is a common German man's name
the Gents is the British name for a men's public lavatory
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A cleaner and the speaker leave a German man standing next to a public lavatory that someone is scratching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' is a person here, the name Dieter, which loses its I. A gents is a British men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a cleaning agent, such as washing-up liquid or laundry powder.

clue.text: Modernist novel's character that could be male or female — Orlando?

definitions.text: Modernist novel's character that could be male or female
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the surname of Leopold and Molly, husband and wife in Joyce's Ulysses
second meaning: the surname of the film actor Orlando

explanation.surface: It asks whether Orlando, Virginia Woolf's modernist hero who changes sex, is the character meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Woolf's Orlando does turn from man to woman, which is the trap; the novel is Joyce's Ulysses, whose surname belongs to both Leopold and Molly, and Orlando is the actor from The Lord of the Rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname is shared by Joyce's married couple in Ulysses and by the English actor Orlando of Pirates of the Caribbean fame.

clue.text: Golfer cries when given the head of 3 wood

parts.note: golfers shout a warning word when a ball heads for people

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so only the opening letter of the referenced answer is kept

parts.note: 3 points to the answer of 3-down, THREE

explanation.surface: A golfer shouts warnings after taking a shot with a 3-wood club.
explanation.walkthrough: A 3-wood is a golf club, so 'wood' looks like part of the golf scene; it is the definition. The 3 is a cross-reference to 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area of trees, which is what a wood is.

clue.text: Fling cat across stage, just missing director

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the animal's letters stretch round the others

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

indicators.note: the platform is only short of one thing, the letter for the person named next

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform
D is the abbreviation for director

explanation.surface: Someone hurls a cat across a theatre stage, narrowly avoiding the director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fling' reads as a verb to throw, but it is the noun for a brief affair. 'Across' tells you the cat's letters span the shortened stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret or short-lived romantic affair, which is what a fling is.

clue.text: Make out in collapsed dune then run to the top of beach

indicators.note: a collapsed heap of sand has lost its shape, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: the letter for running is lifted out of its place and moved to the top of the following word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a strand is a shore or beach

explanation.surface: A couple kiss in a fallen sand dune and then run up to the top of the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' suggests kissing on the beach; it means to grasp. The R already inside STRAND moves to the front of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something can mean to perceive or grasp it, which is what to understand is.

clue.text: Approaches a river in 3 diff erent directions

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the set of compass points that follows

parts.note: 3 refers to 3-down, THREE; three compass points are north, east and south
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone comes towards a river from three separate directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 is a cross-reference to 3-down; the directions are compass points, here N, E and S, with A and R slipped between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To near a place is to draw closer to it, so nears is the same as approaches.

clue.text: Poland's lead runner wearing Polish jacket

indicators.note: something worn is surrounded by clothing, so these letters go inside the polish word

parts.note: a sheen is a polish or gloss, the capital P only disguising it

indicators.note: the lead is what goes first, so just the opening letter of the country is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the country
a ski is a runner on snow

explanation.surface: A Polish athlete, the first one from Poland, is wearing a Polish-made jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the noun for a shine, a classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a coat or jacket made from a sheep's hide with the wool left on.

clue.text: Loiter under the influence alongside taxi car

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: someone under the influence of drink is unsteady and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk hangs around next to a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a convertible.

clue.text: Lout turned up and cooked, enthralling new lover

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning something up flips it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a yob is a loutish youth

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the cooked word holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: fried means cooked in fat
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A thug arrives and makes dinner, charming a new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Yob is British slang for a rowdy, aggressive young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend is a male partner in a romantic relationship, that is, a lover.

clue.text: Both of Lowry's initials around the edges of pristine painting

parts.note: the painter L. S. Lowry, read as L and S
ca. is short for circa, meaning around

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, the first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A clean painting signed with both of the artist Lowry's initials around its border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both of' wants to be two separate letters, but the 'and' between them is spelt out too. L. S. Lowry was an English painter of industrial scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting of countryside or other scenery, as many of Lowry's were.

clue.text: Old Frenchman cutting plant before landlady emptied well

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it, so the Frenchman sits within the plant

parts.note: a tree is a plant
M is short for Monsieur, the French for Mr

indicators.note: an emptied word has had its contents removed, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: only the outside letters survive

explanation.surface: A retired Frenchman is chopping down a plant before his landlady has drained the well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like the water source in the scene; it is the adverb, as in 'well worth it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an intensifier, as in 'well pleased', well means very or to a great degree.

clue.text: We hear about urologist's area of study, leading to boredom

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the phrase that follows is matched by how it is said

parts.note: about means on, as in on a subject, and a urologist studies urine, or wee

explanation.surface: We are told about what a urologist researches, and it turns out to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee is British slang for urine. Said aloud, 'on wee' comes out close to the French loanword.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a feeling of listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a refined word for boredom.

clue.text: Liquid mop has over?

indicators.note: something liquid flows and has no fixed form, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some fluid that a mop of hair gets poured over it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a liquid that your mop, or head of hair, has over it when washed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap used for washing hair, and a mop is a slang word for a head of hair.

clue.text: Get up thanks to this one large branch

parts.note: a means one
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arm is a branch, as of a river or organisation

explanation.surface: You wake thanks to a single big branch, perhaps one tapping at the window.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: the thing that makes you get up in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm clock wakes a sleeper, so it is what makes one rise from bed.

clue.text: Fellow gang member breaking up massive stones

clue.text: Decline to get back together?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to say no, turn down
second meaning, said with a different stress: to join again by melting

explanation.walkthrough: Read as re-fuse, the word means to fuse again; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb refuse means to turn down an offer, while re-fuse means to weld or join once more.

clue.text: Zips zip?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: trouser fastenings, each called a fly

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to zip is to move very fast

explanation.walkthrough: The same word does both jobs: trouser zips are flies, and someone who flies zips along. The question mark covers the loose fit of the two forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly is the zipped opening on trousers, and to fly also means to travel at high speed.

clue.text: Sam Cooke performed this single on the radio

clue.text: A black Vauxhall finally departed in reverse

clue.text: Drink that is, in the morning, nicer combined with a doughnut?

clue.text: Possessed mind does start to envision bats

clue.text: Metal socket's covering something that might be electric
